_readme: Content for the personalized welcome kit popup. /api/welcome merges this with clients.json + codex.json based on the access code. Four maps, one per field Eric's POps tool sends: offering, country, manager, and (via clients.json/codex.json) client. Edit freely. This file is hand-owned, unlike clients.json and codex.json, which are generated snapshots.
_sources: Offerings and manager maps come from public Slack (Aug 2026): #f-talent-general, #f-gtm-general, #f-coordination-general, the People Ops scope thread in #c-avoca, #c-console, #c-modal, plus per-client staffing in codex.json. Country notes are public research and need Eric's sign-off before they ship.

embeddedRecruiting.label: Embedded Recruiting
how: You sit inside the client's team. Their Slack, their Ashby, their hiring meetings. If you're doing it right, the client forgets you're not on their payroll.
Ashby is the ATS and the system of record for every search. Get oriented in week one and ask anything in #g-ashby-support.
The weekly loop is pipeline health, role by role: who's in play, what's stalled, how long candidates have sat idle, which hiring manager owes feedback. Come with the numbers.
Sourcing gets measured. Sequences enrolled, click rate, reply rate, conversion. We A/B test outreach copy and share whatever wins.
Aperture (aperture.is) is our own sourcing and market research tool. Log in with your Carrara Google account and use it for sourcing, company research and talent market questions.
Friday is the Talent Jam. Fill in the Notion agenda before standup and confirm your roles in the Open Roles DB are accurate. New roles and closed hires go in the forms linked there.
#f-talent-general is where the team trades comp data, interview scripts, backchannel asks and process experiments. Use it early.

talentPlatform.label: Talent Platform
how: You're the fractional Head of Talent. The job is the operating system behind hiring, and your audience is the client's leadership, not a req list.
Typical scope: the hiring plan and role prioritization, interview architecture and scorecards, comp bands and leveling, recruiting analytics, agency strategy, ATS build-out.
Comp work comes up constantly. We build bands off three market anchors (frontier labs, same-stage AI, adjacent enterprise SaaS) rather than one source. Pave is a reference point, not the answer.
A lot of the value is upstream. Design the process a hiring manager follows before they ask for headcount, so requests land shaped instead of half-baked.
You'll usually sit on top of an embedded pod. Find out who's sourcing and coordinating on your account before you change anything.

syncWith.name: Joe Penn
syncWith.why: runs the talent side of the business and sets what good looks like on platform engagements

peopleOps.label: People Ops
how: People Ops is everything after someone signs: contracts, onboarding, payroll, benefits, policy, compliance, and the systems holding it together.

The team works from ten focus areas: compliance and risk, payroll and benefits ownership, onboarding operations, the new hire experience, policies and documentation, infrastructure for scale (performance cycles, promotions, comp bands, leveling, org chart), workplace ops, manager and employee support, vendor and tool management, and planning three to six months out.
You own the vendor relationships, not just the tickets. HRIS (Rippling turns up at a lot of our clients), brokers, background checks, PEOs.
You're the first person the client's team asks about benefits, leave and policy, and you coach their managers on escalation paths.
Build light systems that survive you. On most engagements the goal is that the client eventually runs it without us.
Track the boring metrics. Time to onboard, error rates, satisfaction signals. They're how you prove the work landed.

syncWith.name: Kenna Meyerhoff
syncWith.why: leads People at Carrara and owns how we run people work for clients and internally

syncWith.name: Eric Fernandez
syncWith.why: runs internal ops, payroll and systems, so he's the reference point for how this works in practice

finance.label: Finance
how: Engagements run lean, usually one or two people per client, so you'll own a whole workstream instead of a slice of one.

The work splits across embedded finance (bookkeeping, monthly close, AP/AR, management reporting, forecasting, budgeting, KPI dashboards) and strategic finance (unit economics, pricing, capital allocation, board reporting, fundraising and investor readiness).
Transactions are a real part of the job. Recent work carried clients through acquisitions on both sides, including diligence and everything after the deal closed.
Deliverables follow the brand templates in the hub, and every client gets a rolling doc. If you're unsure on scope or billing, ask your client lead before the client asks you.
#z-finance-labs pipes in the CFO newsletters the team reads. Good way to pick up the vocabulary fast.

syncWith.name: Heath Jamieson
syncWith.why: leads the finance accounts and will set your first month's priorities

bizops.label: BizOps
how: BizOps takes the important, cross-functional problems that don't sit neatly in any one department.
You diagnose across product, customers, GTM, operations, finance and org design, find the highest-leverage problem, then go execute against it.

Recent work: a production AI collections agent pulling together eight legacy systems, a relocation marketplace spun out on a 90 day timeline, headcount models, and a BD playbook that got replicated across other clients.
Some engagements are outcome-priced, with a diagnostics fee creditable against outcomes plus a share of savings. Be precise about what you claim.
Expect to work like a fractional Chief of Staff or Head of Ops. Build the process, then run it until it holds without you.

syncWith.name: Heath Jamieson
syncWith.why: leads the bizops book and the venture-style builds

executiveSearch.label: Executive Search
how: High-touch searches for leadership roles the client can't afford to get wrong, usually C-suite, VP, or a specialized senior seat.
You own the whole arc: success profile, market map, network activation, targeted outreach, assessment, references, closing.
These searches almost always grow out of an account we already run, which is the advantage. You start with real context on the client's strategy, culture and leadership gaps instead of a brief.
So your first move isn't the market. It's finding the client lead and absorbing what they already know.

syncWith.name: Joe Penn
syncWith.why: runs the talent side and will point you at the right client lead

gtm.label: Go-to-market
how: GTM covers narrative, comms, content, growth, paid media, events, employer brand and web builds across clients.
Everything you make should feel like the client's brand. Start from their site and brand vault before you write a word.
The weekly GTM sync covers progress, priorities and blockers, and focuses on the accounts without their own sync. Agenda lives in a Slack canvas with a sub-canvas per client.
Keep Linear updated. It's how priorities, resourcing and blockers get tracked, and it feeds the weekly client comms.
Talent Narrative is the crossover product with the talent team: employer brand and hiring story work that runs GTM and Talent together.
Design sits with Yanel and Macarena, and the Carrara design system lives in Figma. Post launches and wins in #g-amplify so the team can boost them.

syncWith.name: Gonz Sanchez
syncWith.why: runs GTM and owns the narrative work and the client relationships across it

coordination.label: Recruiting Coordination
how: Five focus areas: interview coordination, candidate experience, pipeline and process ops, agency logistics, and light workplace support.
You own Ashby scheduling end to end. Screens, panels, onsite loops, reschedules, confirmations, reminders.
ATS hygiene is the job, not admin around the job. Clean statuses, tags and scorecards are what make the client's reporting true.
You're the point of contact for agencies. Track submissions, interview progress, and feedback going back to them.
The coord team has its own weekly and a shared channel in #f-coordination-general. Ask there before inventing a workaround. Someone has usually solved it already.

syncWith.name: Hayley Samuels
syncWith.why: leads coordination, runs the weekly, and will get you onto your client's Ashby

other.label: Your team
how: Your manager will walk you through how your team runs in your day one 1:1.
Default operating mode across Carrara: async first (Loom and Slack), briefs in the Base doc template, Granola on every client call.
Set up the Quarry in week one. Most of how we work assumes it.
Read the Ways of Working page in Notion in week two: the four principles and what they look like in practice.

US.label: United States
notes: Payroll: Deel if you're a full-time employee, Bill.com if you're a US contractor. The invite comes by email. Ping Eric if it hasn't shown up in your first few days.

Contractors: send your W-9 back the same week so your first payment isn't delayed. Your 1099 arrives electronically through Bill.com's tax partner at year end, and you'll get a consent email to accept eDelivery.
Full-time employees complete I-9 employment eligibility verification. Eric sends it over.
As a contractor you handle your own quarterly estimated taxes. We don't withhold anything.
Holidays and time off follow the policy in the Time off section of this hub. Post planned time off in #g-ooo.

AR.label: Argentina
notes: Carrara contracts you in the US and pays you in USD as an independent contractor. There's no Argentine employment relationship, so nothing local gets withheld for you.
Payroll: international contractors run through Ramp. You'll get an invite. Invoice monthly in USD.

Most people here register as monotributista and invoice Carrara with a Factura E, the export of services invoice. Income that counts as a genuine service export doesn't eat into your monotributo billing ceiling.
The BCRA lifted the USD 36,000 annual cap on foreign currency inflows in September 2025, so there's no ceiling on what you can receive.

Plan US travel early. Argentina isn't in the Visa Waiver Program, so ESTA isn't available to you and you'll need a B-1/B-2 visitor visa for offsites or client visits. Restoration talks are paused with no timeline, and appointment waits run long.
Most client work runs on US hours. Agree your overlap window with your manager in week one.
Post planned time off in #g-ooo, including local holidays you plan to take.
confirm: Whether Carrara needs a W-8BEN on file for non-US contractors.
Whether Carrara covers or reimburses the B-1/B-2 visa cost for team offsites.
The invoicing format and monthly cut-off Eric expects.

AU.label: Australia
notes: Carrara contracts you in the US and pays you in USD as an independent contractor, so no Australian employment obligations sit with us.
Payroll: international contractors run through Ramp. You'll get an invite. Invoice monthly in USD.
Most contractors here work as a sole trader with an ABN and invoice against it. You lodge your own return with the ATO and manage PAYG instalments yourself.

GST: you only have to register once turnover hits or is expected to hit A$75,000. Services exported to a non-resident are generally GST-free, so you normally don't add GST to a Carrara invoice even if you're registered. Check your own position with your accountant.
US travel is easy. Australia is in the Visa Waiver Program, so an approved ESTA covers offsites and client meetings as a business visitor.
The timezone gap with the US is real. Agree a standing overlap window with your manager and lean on async (Loom, Slack) for everything else.
Post planned time off in #g-ooo, including local holidays you plan to take.
confirm: Whether Carrara needs a W-8BEN on file for non-US contractors.

CA.label: Canada
notes: Carrara contracts you in the US and pays you in USD as an independent contractor.
Payroll: international contractors run through Ramp. You'll get an invite. Invoice monthly in USD.

You'll likely be asked for a W-8BEN. It certifies you're not a US person, and because you perform the work outside the US the income is foreign-source, so the 30% US withholding doesn't apply. It's valid for three calendar years.
You report the income to CRA as business income on form T2125 and make your own quarterly instalments, since nothing gets withheld at source.

GST/HST: you have to register once taxable supplies pass CAD 30,000 in a quarter or across four consecutive quarters. Services to a US client are zero-rated exports, so you charge 0% but still register and file once you cross that line.
Self-employed contributors pay both halves of CPP. EI is generally optional.
US travel is easy. Canadian citizens are visa-exempt for business visits.
Post planned time off in #g-ooo.
confirm: Whether Carrara needs a W-8BEN on file for non-US contractors.

OTHER.label: Your country
notes: Payroll: international contractors run through Ramp, full-time employees through Deel. Eric will confirm which applies to you.

Carrara contracts you in the US and pays you in USD as an independent contractor, so your local tax registration and filings are yours to manage. Check with a local accountant on how to invoice a foreign client.
Expect to be asked for a W-8BEN so we can document that you're not a US person.
If US travel is likely for offsites or client visits, check early whether your passport is Visa Waiver eligible or whether you need a B-1/B-2 appointment. Waits can run months.
Agree your overlap window with your manager in week one if your client runs on US hours.
Post planned time off in #g-ooo.
confirm: The country-specific payment rail and paperwork. Eric confirms this case by case.
